name: agentgrade
description: Grades how well AI assistants and answer engines can find, read, understand, and cite a website, with step-by-step fixes.

interface.longDescription:
AgentGrade grades how well AI assistants, AI search, and answer engines can find, read, understand, and cite a website.

Give it any public URL. It fetches the page, robots.txt, sitemap, and llms.txt the way an AI crawler does, without running JavaScript, and returns an A-F grade with a 0-100 score across nine categories: crawlability, understanding, answer readiness, citability, trust, content depth, freshness, AI-native signals, and real-user performance from the Chrome UX Report.

It shows which AI crawlers robots.txt allows or blocks, ranks every issue by impact, and gives a plain-language fix for each one, with a copy-paste code snippet where one applies. The grade is weighted for the kind of page it is, so a homepage is not marked down for lacking an article's FAQ or publish date.

AgentGrade reads public pages only and never changes anything. No account or sign-in is needed. The full methodology is published at agentgrade.app/methodology.
capabilities: Grade any public web page for AI visibility, A to F
Score nine categories, from crawlability to real-user performance
Show which AI crawlers robots.txt allows or blocks
List every issue with a step-by-step fix and code snippet
defaultPrompt: Can AI assistants read and cite my website?
Which AI crawlers does my site block?
Give me every fix to make my site easier for AI to cite

positive.description: Grade a well-known site for AI visibility.
positive.prompt: Can ChatGPT and other AI tools actually read and cite stripe.com? Grade it.
positive.expected_behavior: Calls grade_site with stripe.com and reports the overall letter grade and score, the nine category grades, which AI crawlers robots.txt allows, and the top fixes.

positive.description: A business owner asks why AI tools do not mention their site.
positive.prompt: Why doesn't ChatGPT ever mention my business? My website is lilagents.com.
positive.expected_behavior: Calls grade_site with lilagents.com and explains the grade and the highest-impact issues in plain language, with the fix for each.

positive.description: Follow up a grade with the complete fix list.
positive.prompt: Now give me the complete list of fixes for stripe.com, most severe first.
positive.expected_behavior: Calls get_fixes for stripe.com and lists every issue most severe first, each with what was found, how to fix it, and any code snippet.

positive.description: Check which AI crawlers a site blocks.
positive.prompt: Which AI crawlers does linkedin.com block in its robots.txt?
positive.expected_behavior: Calls grade_site with linkedin.com and names each AI crawler (such as GPTBot, ClaudeBot, and PerplexityBot) and whether robots.txt allows or blocks it.

positive.description: Get fixes for one category only.
positive.prompt: Just show me the structured data and metadata fixes for python.org.
positive.expected_behavior: Calls get_fixes with python.org and the understanding category, and lists only those issues with their fixes.

negative.description: A general writing request unrelated to websites.
negative.prompt: Write a short poem about autumn in Seattle.

negative.description: A coding question that does not involve grading a site.
negative.prompt: How do I reverse a linked list in Python?

negative.description: A question about a website's business, not its AI visibility.
negative.prompt: What does Stripe charge per credit card transaction?

publication.release_notes: First release. Two read-only tools: grade_site returns an A-F AI-visibility grade across nine categories with the top fixes, and get_fixes lists every issue with a step-by-step fix.
